summary: A Go MCP server that gives Claude Code and other AI hosts your own tools, built as one binary they start over stdio.
description: Start a Model Context Protocol server in Go on the official Go library. One unit-conversion tool proves the shape: its input and output are Go structs whose JSON Schemas the library derives, arguments are checked before the handler runs, and a caller's mistake comes back as a tool error the model can read and fix, while server faults and panics hide their cause and go to the log. Logs are JSON on stderr and a lint rule keeps prints off stdout, which belongs to the protocol. Tests call the tools through a real client in memory and by starting the built binary, and a dev client calls tools from the shell. It ships no remote HTTP transport, authentication or storage.
seoDescription: A Go MCP server recipe on the official Go library: typed stdio tools with JSON Schemas from structs, readable tool errors and protocol tests.

projectExamples.title: Internal docs lookup for a coding assistant
projectExamples.description: Illustrative: replace the conversion tool with search and fetch tools over the team's docs, so Claude Code can look things up. Access control and indexing are still the project's work.

plain.whatItIs: A starter Go program that AI coding assistants such as Claude Code run in the background to call tools you write, like a plugin.
goodAt: Giving an AI assistant actions or lookups written in Go
